methods.summary: Run a checkpointed, reorg-aware indexer over decoded events.
methods.description:
Run a checkpointed, reorg-aware indexer over decoded events.

Write your rows in `onBatch` and commit `ctx.cursor` in the same transaction; resume with `fromCursor`. Without `fromCursor` or `fromHeight` the API serves only its recent default window, so pass `fromHeight: 0` for a full backfill. A reorg at or below your checkpoint calls `onReorg`, then the loop re-reads from the fork point. Delivery is at-least-once, so keep writes idempotent. With a `sink`, the checkpoint and rollback are handled for you. `finalizedOnly` holds delivery to finalized rows, so no reorg handling is needed. `mode: "tail"` (default) keeps polling at the tip; `mode: "bounded"` returns on the first empty page. Resolves to `{ cursor, pages, emptyPolls }`.

fields.description:

fields.name: commitBatch
fields.type: (cursor: string, write: (tx: Tx) => Promise<void> | void) => Promise<void>
fields.description:
Apply one batch atomically: open a transaction, run `write(tx)` (the
user's inserts), and commit the rows AND `cursor` together. A throw
from `write` must abort the whole transaction — leaving neither rows
nor cursor, so a crashed batch is simply re-read on restart.

fields.name: rollback
fields.description:
Roll the projection back to the fork: delete everything AT OR ABOVE
`forkPointHeight` (inclusive `>=` — the new chain re-supplies the fork
block) and commit `rewindCursor` in the SAME transaction. Deleting
without the rewound cursor is the classic silent-gap bug: a crash
between the two writes resumes above the fork and the deleted range is
never re-read.

On a multi-fork page this is called once PER fork, every call with the
same `rewindCursor` (the lowest fork point) but its own
`forkPointHeight` — scope the undo by `forkPointHeight` only (contract
invariant #11), and expect re-application after a crash (#10).

`rewindCursor` is `null` only for a fork at genesis: clear the
checkpoint so the next run starts from the first event.
